overview: Two reproductive strategies that trade off speed and uniformity against genetic diversity.
genZNote: Asexual: control-C, control-V yourself. Sexual: mixing two playlists into one.

aspects.label: Gamete Formation
aspects.valueB: Involves formation and fusion of male and female gametes.

aspects.label: Genetic Variation
aspects.valueA: Offspring are genetically identical clones of the parent.
aspects.valueB: Offspring are genetically unique, combining traits from both parents.

aspects.label: Speed / Energy Cost
aspects.valueA: Fast and energy-efficient; no need to find a mate.
aspects.valueB: Slower and more energy-costly, but improves adaptability.

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueA: Binary fission in bacteria, budding in yeast, vegetative propagation in plants.
aspects.valueB: Fertilisation in humans, flowering plants, and most animals.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Sexual reproduction's main evolutionary advantage is variation, which helps populations survive changing environments.
overlay.memoryTrick: Asexual = one parent, exact copy. Sexual = two parents, unique mix.
overlay.commonMisconception: Asexual reproduction is not 'primitive' or inferior — many highly successful organisms rely on it exclusively.
